desc:
CRM automation for contacts, deals and tasks keeps your sales records current without anyone typing them in twice. Ecom Swift LLC builds rules inside your own CRM that create contacts, move deals, assign owners, add follow-up tasks and flag quiet deals.

## What is CRM automation?

CRM automation is a set of rules that update your customer records when something happens. A form fills in, an email arrives, a deal changes stage or a week passes with no contact, and the CRM responds on its own. It might create a contact, assign a sales rep, add a task, move a deal or send an alert.

The aim is a CRM that reflects reality, so the pipeline you see is the pipeline you have.

## Why CRMs go stale

A CRM is only as good as its last update. Salespeople are busy talking to customers, and typing notes is the first thing to slide. Leads come in from forms, email, ads and events, and each is entered differently, or not at all. Within months the system holds duplicates, missing owners and deals stuck in a stage they left weeks ago.

At that point the team stops trusting it and goes back to spreadsheets and memory. Forecasts become guesses, follow-ups are missed and a lead that asked for a quote goes cold because nobody knew it was waiting.

## What changes when the CRM updates itself

The biggest gain is speed to the first contact. When a new lead is created, assigned and given a task within moments, someone calls or writes while interest is fresh. Assignment rules make sure no lead is left without an owner, and round-robin sharing spreads the work fairly.

A second gain is discipline without nagging. Task sequences after each new lead mean steps are not forgotten. Alerts on quiet deals bring forward the ones slipping away. Clean, current data also makes reports meaningful, since stage counts and owner lists mean what they say.

## What a great CRM rule set includes

- Automatic contact creation from forms, email and other lead sources.
- A duplicate check before a new record is added.
- Owner assignment by region, product or round-robin.
- Deal stage changes triggered by real events.
- Follow-up tasks with sensible due dates.
- Alerts on deals with no activity for a set time.
- A simple lead score based on rules you choose.
- Notes added automatically from forms and messages.
- A weekly pipeline summary for the team.
- Written documentation of every rule.

## How we build it

We begin by sitting down with your pipeline: the stages, who owns each, what must happen at each step and where leads come from. We write the rules in plain words and ask you to correct them. Only then do we build, working inside your own CRM account.

Before anything touches live records, we test on a copy or with clearly marked sample data. After approval we switch on the rules one group at a time and check the results. Basic creates contacts from one source, adds one follow-up task and assigns an owner by a simple rule. Standard adds more lead sources, stage rules, task sequences, quiet-deal alerts and a duplicate check. Premium adds round-robin assignment, scoring, a weekly pipeline email and a team training call. We do not delete or rewrite existing records without your approval.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Define your pipeline stages clearly before building.
- Decide what counts as a duplicate.
- Keep rules simple and named in plain words.
- Tell us which lead sources are most valuable.
- Train the team on what the automation does.

**Avoid:**
- Moving deals automatically on weak signals.
- Creating tasks nobody has time to complete.
- Layering rules that contradict each other.
- Skipping a copy test before going live.
- Ignoring the alerts once they start arriving.

## Who it is for

A small sales team whose leads arrive from a website form, email and events, and who spend Fridays updating records. A service business that wants every enquiry assigned and followed up the same day. A founder who sells alone and wants the CRM to remind them of deals before they go cold.

## What we need from you

Tell us which CRM you use, your pipeline stages, your lead sources and who should own what. Share any current rules so we do not duplicate them. We work as a collaborator, staff or admin-limited user in your own account, never ask for passwords, and you keep full ownership of the CRM and every rule we create. Questions about data privacy rules remain your decision, and we follow the settings you choose.
